note: Every model in the summary table is a single run. Nemotron is the only one run repeatedly. These are those runs, all on the identical four tasks with the identical hidden suites.

abgleich_series.question: Does asking the model to check the task statement point by point before finishing help?
abgleich_series.verdict: No effect measurable — and the series could not have measured one: 17 of 40 task runs hit the 80-turn limit, so the binding constraint was the turn budget, not the mechanism. The check itself costs turns from that same budget.
abgleich_series.harness_gap: One task run in the "mit" arm (round 5, t1-debug) ended with zero tool calls and was accepted as finished, scoring 9/15 on an untouched seed. That is a harness gap, not a model result, and it depresses that round by roughly six points. jaja now nudges once in that case.

Nemotron-3.5-Lightning.note: three harness/engine configurations plus the ten-run Abgleich series

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4).note: Two Java-harness runs and one opencode run, same model, same quantisation. t2-refactor came out 16/17, 0/17 and 17/17. The opencode run is the fastest perfect run in the collection at 21:01.

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (FP8 vs NVFP4).note: Same model, two precisions, two harnesses. t2-refactor across the four: 0, 16, 0, 17. Any claim about what quantisation costs can be supported or refuted here by choosing which runs to quote.
